recommendation: Keep the fix as-is. The WG decision did not rename the elements, and this reconciliation completes the intended wording clarification in the active core StructureDefinition source.
issue_request: FHIR-46911 was Applied as Not Persuasive with Modification for R6. The requester found MedicationAdministration.isSubPotent confusing when paired with the description 'Full dose was not administered' and noted the related subPotentReason element; Pharmacy kept the subPotent clinical term but voted to clarify the description using the ordered-dose meaning.
initial_application: The original application commit be847eb09f2234df9555e6f35a2256a794d5ad9a changed only MedicationAdministration.isSubPotent.short to 'An indication that the full ordered dose was not administered'. It left isSubPotent.definition and both subPotentReason strings using the old 'full dose' wording.
additional_context: MedicationAdministration is active in source/fhir.ini. The May 2025 Pharmacy WG minutes record that 'full dose' was ambiguous between the intended 'full ordered dose' and a typical or usual guideline dose, and that the motion to add 'ordered' passed. Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: Updated source/medicationadministration/structuredefinition-MedicationAdministration.xml so isSubPotent.definition, subPotentReason.short, and subPotentReason.definition consistently say 'full ordered dose'.
source_changes: source/medicationadministration/structuredefinition-MedicationAdministration.xml: changed MedicationAdministration.isSubPotent.definition to 'An indication that the full ordered dose was not administered.'
source/medicationadministration/structuredefinition-MedicationAdministration.xml: changed MedicationAdministration.subPotentReason short and definition to refer to the full ordered dose.
